title: It was a merchant's mark, centuries before email.
description:
It was a merchant's mark, centuries before email. It meant 'at the rate of': three crates @ two shillings. A trader's shorthand for a price, not a piece of computer punctuation.

A Florentine merchant wrote the earliest known @ (standing in for an amphora, a unit of wine) in a letter about treasure the conquistadors shipped from Peru. In Spanish and Portuguese the sign is still 'arroba,' a unit of weight.

@ had sat on typewriter keyboards since the 1880s. Little used, always there. Which is exactly why it was free for the taking when networks needed a character that would never turn up inside someone's name.

Ray Tomlinson grabbed @ to split the name from the machine. It was not an assignment: he was fooling around with ARPANET. He needed one symbol to mean this user at this computer, and @ already meant at. The address bar has looked that way ever since.

A mark for pricing wine now sits in New York's Museum of Modern Art, credited to Tomlinson.

Sources:
- https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/104059-first-instance-of-at-sign: Guinness World Records, read in full. Establishes: per history professor Giorgio Stabile (La Sapienza, Rome), the first documented, credible appearance of @ dates to 4 May 1536, when Italian merchant Francesco Lapi used it to stand for an amphora (a unit of measurement) in a letter about treasure shipped by the conquistadors from Peru; earlier medieval-scribe uses arguably exist, but Lapi's is the first known use of @ as a character with a distinct meaning; an amphora was a wine vessel that became a unit of volume; @ evolved into shorthand for 'at' and appeared on typewriter keyboards in the 1880s; and the first use of @ in email dates to 1971.
- https://gulfnews.com/world/americas/ray-tomlinson-inventor-of-email-and--symbol-dies-1.1685430: Associated Press obituary of Ray Tomlinson (via Gulf News), read in full. Establishes: Tomlinson invented the first network person-to-person email in 1971 on ARPANET; it was not an assignment ('he was just fooling around'), the first messages went between two machines side by side and were 'entirely forgettable'; he chose the @ symbol to connect the username with the destination address; and in 2010 MoMA's Department of Architecture and Design added the @ symbol to its collection, crediting Tomlinson.
- https://www.britannica.com/topic/at-sign: Encyclopaedia Britannica, read (summary/lead). Corroborates that before the late 20th century the @ sign's primary use was commercial, signifying 'at the rate of,' and that it traces to the amphora/arroba unit of measure.
